Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were working as a uniformed police officer, you personally never received orders from persons at the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Especially while you were working as a uniformed police officer, you never received orders from the then-minister of the interior of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that you never submitted reports to the minister -- Ministry of Interior or the then-minister, that would also be correct. You personally never submitted such reports, did you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, I never did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the question of my learned friend the Prosecutor, you also said that for a while you were a member of a Posebna police unit.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of that police unit your battalion commander was Ljupco Bliznakovski; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ljupco Bliznakovski, to your best knowledge, as a member of his battalion, was a police officer with a great deal of experience and is considered a good professional. Is that -- are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat the answer closer to the microphone and louder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ljupco Bliznakovski was considered a good professional, a police officer with a great deal of experience at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that for this reason he was subsequently appointed deputy assistant minister of the interior for the city of Skopje, and in 2001, he was responsible for the uniformed police in the sector of internal affairs for the city of Skopje. Are you familiar with this fact?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I recall -- I don't recall the exact period of time when that was, but you could remind me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Likewise, answering the questions asked by my learned friend, you said that later on, you were transferred from the Posebna unit to a police station, and then at some time you were part of the security of -- for the minister of the interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I remember well, you also said that this had happened around about May 2001. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, that was a time when Mr. Boskoski was appointed minister of the interior. Is that about that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that -- that you were actually selected from among five candidates who wanted to be members of the ministry security?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask again the witness to please speak up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking to move -- asking you to move closer to the microphone so that they may hear you better, and that was also my request to you, and please answer the questions more clearly so we may understand you better. When you became a member of the security of the minister of the interior in 2001, there was already a crisis situation in the Republic of Macedonia due to terrorist attacks committed by Albanian terrorists and extremists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you agree with me, as you had been a police officer before, that those were very difficult times to do police work?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, the police, in addition to their routine, work and tasks as laid down by the law was also required to engage in some combat activity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That period was especially difficult for the police, as it was police stations and police patrols that were frequently the targets of terrorist attacks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the terrorists also attacked civilian population and army positions, as well as journalists. Do you remember that the attacks were targeted against those also?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a person who was near the minister - I'm not saying close - but you were near him as his body-guard, you were certainly in a position to know and see in the field that police frequently participated in joint activities with the army of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It could also be known to you, and now I'm asking whether that is really so, that at that time a significant number of police officers were wounded or killed in terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This situation provoked revolt on the population so that demonstrations were occurring, which resulted in additional obligations for the police. Have there been such demonstrations of which you know?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There were such events, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a part of the book written by Minister Boskoski, My Struggle -- or My Fight for Macedonia, and you said that you did not personally witness large-scale demonstrations in the month of June in the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But let me ask you whether it is correct that on numerous occasions when there were protests by the population, the police took measures, to protect those parts of the city where ethnic Albanians lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I would like to put the following to you, and please say if I'm right in saying that the -- the police in Macedonia, on the whole, strove to protect all citizens irrespective of their ethnic affiliation, be they -- whether they were ethnic Macedonians, Albanians, Turks, Bosniaks or others?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a man who was near Minister Boskoski, were you able to see that Minister Boskoski took equal care for all citizens of Macedonia and that he did not discriminate among them in any way?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend the Prosecutor showed you an extract from the book written by Mr. Boskoski, and he read out the section which says that during the crisis, Mr. Boskoski practically worked round the clock. But in that same section, I'm now going to read this out to you: [In English] "These were the days in which I was working until the last atom in my body. My alertness and engagement could not be measured by 24 or 48 hours, but by series of nights and days without sleep. Yet, with an unbreakable desire in the fight for Macedonia mainly, owing to my young age, stamina and my unshakeable Macedonian patriotism in which there is room for every human being for all the citizens of whatever ethnic or religious group if they sincerely and truly loved Macedonia." [Interpretation] Tell me, please, to the best of your understanding and in accordance with what you heard from Mr. Boskoski, was this not his basic message to all of you, that you should take care for every human being and all citizens irrespective of their ethnic or religious affiliations. So all those who loved their country, Macedonia. Were you able to notice that this was the attitude held by Mr. Boskoski toward all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also showed you a section of the book written by Mr. Boskoski which displays his emotional attitude toward the events. This is not a documentary book but he pointed out a fact mentioned in that book that Mr. Boskoski allegedly left the coordinating body and in his stead, Mr. Refet Elmazi was appointed to that position. You said that you didn't know whether Mr. Boskoski had left that coordinating body or not and I'm not going to ask you about that because you have already testified to that. But let me ask you: Did you know, in 2001, that Refet Elmazi was Mr. Boskoski's deputy, so that he was actually the deputy minister of the interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you know that Mr. Refet Elmazi was an ethnic Albanian; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you're also aware that for the entire duration of the crisis and that for the entire duration of the term of office Mr. Boskoski, Refet Elmazi was and remained deputy to the minister of the interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can surely testify that the Minister Boskoski and his deputy Refet Elmazi were then and later in a good relation, one could say, a friendly, cordial relation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And with regards to this question, I would like to ask you the following. Are you aware, actually, that Mr. Boskoski was born in the village of Celopek, where Macedonians and Albanians used to live together and they still live together there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I have been there on many occasions and I can give you an example. In the middle of the war when passing through the village when the situation was worse, the minister greeted a senior citizen, an Albanian, and a picture of that was taken for the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when Mr. Boskoski would go to the field, and my learned friend asked you about it, he would greet absolutely in the same way both the police officers, the Macedonian citizens and the citizens who were Albanians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, especially in the village of Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me also ask you whether you remember that at the time Mr. Boskoski was known to go to an ethnic Albanian village himself to speak to the population there, although others held the opinion that he shouldn't be doing that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Several times, to several places.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned friend asked you about Mr. Boskoski's frequent -- frequent travels to the field, you said that he met all sorts of people there. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say to you, sir, that when Mr. Boskoski would go to the field where joint operations are -- were carried out by the army and the police, do you agree that he went there only to provide moral support to his police officers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me put it like this: As his body-guard, when you were also in the field, you never heard him giving orders either to police chiefs or regular police officers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can I then say in conclusion that Minister Boskoski respected all those who were really in charge of operations on the ground and gave orders, et cetera, and that he never interfered with their work?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me also ask you about something that my learned friend the Prosecutor was also interested in, namely, whether you personally liked or disliked Minister Boskoski. Eventually, you said you admired him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: As my superior and as a person, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And explaining the reasons, you said that he was actually a good person. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say that many people considered Mr. Boskoski a good person would also be correct, isn't it -- wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could say that for a -- for a man and a minister he was a very emotional person; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And whenever he would receive information that a police officer had been wounded or killed, that he would take it very personally; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But isn't it also correct that he would always repeat that the police shouldn't react in the same manner and that he was totally free from any revengism [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That attitude toward wounded or killed police officers was also reflected in -- in allowing the family members of the -- these killed police officers to use his weekend cottage in Croatia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes. While I was there, two or three families were there, families consisting of several members.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were in Celopek with the minister, so that was his native village, when his relatives had been killed by terrorists, and when he was saying to the population -- to the villagers that those killings had been committed by terrorists and that was hard on the ethnic Albanians too, because sometimes the terrorist would say use force against Albanians too. Do you remember that occasion, when the minister went to Celopek?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And -- excuse me, what was your answer to my question? I asked you whether you remembered the occasion when you went to Celopek with the minister and you answered? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the transcript there was a negative answer. My learned friend also showed a section of the book to you, a section which says that for the fourth time an assassination of Minister Boskoski had been attempted. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that when you confirmed that you were in -- in Matejce, when you visited the regular police station in Matejce, and you thought that there was no danger there.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is so. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you body-guards always required the minister when he was going near places where there was gun-fire to wear protective equipment and protect himself. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your basic duty was to protect the minister's life, isn't it -- wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although at the time you had information from the army of Macedonia that Matejce was a safe environment and that you could visit the police station there, you were actually attacked fiercely by terrorist groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, this video is -- is Exhibit P401. Due to the wish of the minister to provide moral support to his police officers when they were going to the field, you had problems not only in Matejce but also at other places with guaranteeing his safety; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And answering to the Prosecutor's question, you said that you executed orders received from Zoran Trajkovski, the head of the minister's security. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But if the minister would require you to do something, you would try to do so, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But that isn't only your position as a body-guard. Other body-guards, those of the president of the republic or the Speaker of parliament or other ministers also had to follow orders given to them by their chief of security, but also the personality who they protected. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if it the Speaker of parliament would say to his body-guard to accompany him to a certain place or do something, that body-guard would have to do so, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor asked you about Johan Tarculovski, you said that he was your colleague because he also worked for the Ministry of the Interior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you will also agree that the body-guards of all cabinet ministers and the president were officers of the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put to you that they were only technically officers of the Ministry of Interior, de jure, but that in reality they executed orders of the persons they protected or their chiefs, or superiors that would also be correct, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think, with respect to this witness, it might be appropriate to ask the witness whether he understands what the term "de jure" means, before he is able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did translate that. I said in reality de jure, in reality. So the witness can -- I believe the witness can understand what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is a very technical term, and you would want us to understand it, I think, in a technical sense. So I would suggest you need to be much more careful with the question if you want us to be taking notice of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you..

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again. I'll phrase it differently. In life, in reality, did you as a body-guard and your colleagues who protected other important personalities in the Republic of Macedonia were you employed by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that in reality, on a daily basis, you executed orders given to you by your immediate superior and the person you protected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you could say that you were, in fact, officers of the Ministry of Interior, but that your real superiors, your real bosses were the persons that you protected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to the questions asked to you by my learned friend, the questions about your -- the statement that you had given to the investigators of this Tribunal, I would like to ask you some questions also. As far as I remember, you answered my learned friend that you were questioned very long by the investigators of this Tribunal. Could you say for how many hours you testified, giving the statement that was submitted -- that was shown to you today?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: For more than 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember which year it was when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: 2003 or 4. I don't recall precisely. 2003, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your statement was shown to you. If that statement is dated April the 20th, 2001, then that would certainly be a mistake. It would have to be 2003 or 4.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: 2003, yes, it's like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I assist? If it would be of assistance, on the interpreter's certification page, it is dated 20 April 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has also shown the last page to you with the -- with the interpreter's certification and do you remember the 10th page of the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Actually, I was referring to the witness acknowledgment, not the interpreter's certification. Do you remember the Prosecutor showing you that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today this interpreter certification was also shown to you and it is in Macedonian, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is again a mistake in the translation of what I'm asking. It is not the interpreter's certificate, but the witness acknowledgment. When giving your testimony to the investigator of the ICTY, is it correct that you were asked questions in the English language, that you would reply in Macedonian, and that there was interpreting through interpreters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the end of that entire interview, you actually signed the statement in the English language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you yourself do not speak the English language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, actually, this witness acknowledgment was signed by you in the English language and not in the Macedonian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification, in the transcript it reads that my colleague has asked the witness whether he signed in the English language. I'm just trying to understand. We see a signature here but I'm not sure, and it may be because my linguistic knowledge is not great, but does my learned colleague actually refer to the alphabet that is signed or is she actually referring to a language because in the mind of the Prosecution a signature -- a name is a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood the counsel to be referring to the version of the statement, whether it was the English language version or the Macedonian language version, which was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, sir, Mr. Jakovoski, your statement that you have signed in 2004, at the moment of your signing was in the English language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And before your arrival to The Hague, you haven't seen that statement in the Macedonian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I'm seeing it for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that statement shown to you today, the statement that you have read now in the Macedonian language, was never signed by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Several times, when my learned friend the Prosecutor showed you some parts of your previous statement, you stated: "I had told you earlier that I do not recall some of the events and that they're not as I spoke about them," if I understood that well. I'm only trying to reframe part of your statement. Have I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me apart from this event in April of 2004 when you made your statement to the ICTY investigator, did you have any interviews with the investigator of the Prosecutor afterwards, because this is what I gather from your statement?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this was on a number of occasions on his initiative, not on mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me, did you speak on the phone or would you meet with the investigator?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: On -- by telephone at least five, six times, my private phone. Otherwise, on his initiative, once in Skopje in the Holiday Inn hotel. This was, for me, a psychological problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you then speak only about some technical aspects of your travel, or did you discuss the case, the actual contents of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: In -- in most of the situations by telephone and in the hotel where we met, most was about the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you stated that you would say to the -- you have said to the Prosecutor earlier that what you had stated in your testimony is not completely accurate or that you do not remember some situations, did you also say this to the investigator when you spoke with him on the phone or when you met him in Holiday Inn hotel?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I told him the same when we spoke on the phone and in the hotel when we met, that I do not recall and that the statement is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the transcript, I wish to note that the Defence has received, until the present day, only the statement of this witness of 28th of April, 2004 and it was never informed that the Prosecution had any other interviews on any other occasions with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that when asked by my learned friend you stated that you had said previously that there were issues you did not remember, is it then true, Mr. Jakovoski, that upon giving your statement in 2004, you stated to the investigator several times that you could not remember precisely the events and that it is difficult for to you describe the situation that took place then at that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, and the statements says, writes that I do not recall ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement shown to you today, and I will ask that the witness is shown the first page, 65 ter 1D498, that is 1D4523 in the English, while the Macedonian is -- I apologise. 1D4536, and I would like to ask if the witness could be provided with a copy that the Prosecutor just gave me a while ago, so I would like to ask the usher to give this statement to the witness in the Macedonian language. Tell me, the investigator who interviewed you in 2004, as it is stated on the first page, is Kuehnel Thomas. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me please, who was the investigator who spoke with you over the phone or with whom you met, as you have just testified, in the hotel in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: The same, the investigator Kuehnel Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask now that the witness is shown page 1D4539, Macedonian, item 10, and 1D4540, item 11. Okay, let's see the item 10 first, and the English is 1D4526. Also, again, item 10. In the item 10, can you see in front of you that item 10? You can find the item 10 also in the hard copy that you have in front of you. It states the following: [In English] "On the day before this picture was taken, Saturday." [Interpretation] But I need to say immediately that in the translation into Macedonian there is a mistake, because it says instead of Saturday which should be Sabota, it states Sunday. So here it is stated: [In English] "On the day before this picture was taken, Saturday, I can't remember what we have done. I have problems to answer the question that I have done five days before the events. These days were too busy." [Interpretation] Is this what is written here actually a corroboration of your answer to the Prosecutor's question, that you also stated to the investigator that due to the numerous tasks and duties you could not remember precisely of all the events and actions that took place in the course of those days?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is why I have stated this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you were to look now at item 11, it is in the same page in the English version, while in Macedonian it is in 1D4540, you said again, could you look at this sentences: [In English] "Two days before this picture was taken, Friday, I can't remember what we have done on these days." [Interpretation] Is this also a corroboration that you spoke to the investigator on several occasions that you could not remember all the events?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The paragraph that my learned colleague is reading from, and -- which is paragraph 11, the first sentence, my colleague read into the record, "Two days before this picture was taken, Friday, what we have done on this day. Normally, we started at 8.00 a.m. I know I was on work." I --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I've now lost the LiveNote, I'm sorry. My point is simply this. In the witness's statement he refers to: "I do not remember any event on this day," singular. He did not say "on these days." And at least that is how it came out in the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Maybe I misread the English word and this is why it was entered like that in the transcript. It is it true, it says: [In English] "I can't remember what we have done on this day. Normally we started at 8.00. I know I was on work. I don't remember any events on this day". [Interpretation] Of course, in the item before the witness has already confirmed he could not remember what happened five days ago and not only on that actual date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So my question is very simple. Is it true, as you have testified today, answering the questions of my learned friend, that you said to the investigator in 2004 and also later, and you said often repeated that you could not remember precisely the events or what you were actually doing at a given time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that you were under certain pressure by the events that were taking place at that time in Macedonia because there was a change of power, of government. I would like to ask you whether it is correct that actually during that time many police officers were laid off?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is correct that they were either dismissed or demoted to much junior ranks, people who were, in a way, close to the Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that that was also a pressure on you because you were a police officer and you did not have any other occupation that you could do, other than being a police officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you whether today, because of the change of power again, your situation is such that you were again modifying your testimony and you stated that it was not like that in the least. Nobody asked you to say anything different from the truth before this Court. Actually, nobody asked you anything; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what you are testifying today before this Court you are aware, and the Prosecutor cautioned you several times, that you are testifying under oath?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Although you stated to the investigator of the OTP several times that you could not remember certain events, answering to Prosecutor's question you mentioned, if I understood you well, that the investigator kept repeating the names of Bucuk and Johan. Tell me, were you expected to remember some events or -- despite the fact that you stated that you could not remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, and on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could that be the reason for a certain untrue notions or discrepancies finding a way in your testimony and you then clarified this before the Court today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think this question now goes into the realm of speculation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do you want me to give a comment or to continue questioning the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To give a comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness explained when asked by the Prosecutor, I do not have the actual page of LiveNote where he stated this, that the investigator kept repeating those names to him, and I just asked the witness whether he had the feeling that he is expected, although he said that there was no pressure on him. I can withdraw this question. Maybe this would be the best way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now to look into your statement. It is the page 1D498, 1D453, item 5. The last paragraph in the English page is 1D4525, item 5. Could you please look at the last paragraph where the following is stated: "On the date when this video was recorded, I was with Marian Medarov, Branko Pejcinovski and Laste Mitkov. Being asked where Zoran Trajkovski was during these three days, I can say I don't know where he was at the time in general and on Sunday, when the video material was produced." You know Zoran Trajkovski, isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was your direct superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when asked by the Prosecutor, you could not remember where your direct superior had been then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Zoran Trajkovski himself in his statement to the Prosecutor were to say that he been in the Republic of Croatia at that time, you would not dispute this but you simply do not remember that. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Branko Pejcinovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Branko Pejcinovski was actually a deputy to Zoran Trajkovski during his absence. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask now that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D497, page 1D4518, item 11. This is the statement only in the English page, and I will read it to you. In this statement, Branko Pejcinovski says: [In English] "On 10, 11, 12 August 2001, I was always on duty. I was in charge of the team of the body-guard. Zoran Trajkovski was in Croatia at this time." [Interpretation] Do you agree with me that this statement of Branko Pejcinovski was correct, but you simply at the time when you gave the statement, could not recall where your superior was at that moment? Would that be so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we -- if you look, once again, item 10 of your statement, which is on page 1D418, page 1D4539, the 65 ter 1D498, page 4539, where it was stated that there is a mistake in the translation into the Macedonian language instead of Saturday, it is listed as Sunday, and the English version on page 1D4526. You said at that time that you were at the funeral -- that you were attending a funeral that day with the minister. Do you see this? Do you see that you have stated that at that time? Do you see that you have -- that this is written?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question. I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In effect, here, in item 10, in the middle of it, when you're speaking about what you were doing on -- in -- on Saturday, first you said that you do not know what you were doing, then for five days, and then you say the following: [In English] "I knew that we were with the minister on the funeral." [Interpretation] That is to say, you said that you were attending a funeral with the minister. Do you see that this is written here?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that in front of this Chamber, the witness Risto Galevski said that on Saturday, the 11th of August, he was in Radusa where terrorist groups attacked the police station, and that the Minister Boskoski was in Radusa as well, you could then agree with me that General Galevski had better recollection of this event than you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Recalling when giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me there's a fault in the logic of this question which can only confuse the witness, because nowhere has it been established that Minister Boskoski could have been attending a funeral on Saturday, August 11th, and travel to the area of Radusa and come back to Skopje. So I think that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is one or other.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one and the other can be. I agree with you on one day, the minister can be in two places at one time. But in having in mind that I'm questioning the witness on the issue on his recollection, what he really recalls and what he said at the time when he was giving his statement, in this regard, I would ask him not only this question about Radusa but also additional questions which would clarify to the fact whether the witness at the time when giving the statement he recalled these events or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned colleague is asking the witness to comment on the recollection powers of General Galevski. That's what the last question asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I suggest you find out what this witness says he was doing, if he recalls, whether or not he agrees that he said that the -- your client was at a funeral on the day, and I don't really know you need to take it beyond that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I want -- this is in fact what I want to suggest to the witness, that the minister was not attending any kind of funeral on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, put that to the witness and see if he then has an explanation for the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard the suggestions of the Court. I want to ask you the following now: Is it correct that you and Minister Boskoski did not attend a funeral in the village of Ljubanci on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I can clarify. It must be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is your clarification?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Explain.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I can explain. I have mentioned this funeral because it has nothing to do with the 11th or the days before, but I wanted to say to the investigator that there was too much work on those days and this is why I can't remember. On the 11th, I can agree with the counsel that I went to Radusa on that day with the minister, but then I couldn't remember because the investigation was rather tense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a comment, Your Honour. My learned colleague's question pointedly asked this witness: Is it correct that you and Minister Boskoski did not attend a funeral in the village of Ljubanci, on the 11th of August, and my concern is simply that nowhere in the witness's statement in that paragraph does he mention where such a funeral took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to continue with my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 11th, on Saturday, you did not attend any kind of funeral?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: On the 11th, we did not go to any kind of funeral. On the 11th, we were in Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you spoke about a funeral, as you tried to explain to us now, you remembered that you were at some funeral, and if I say to that you that it was the funeral of a policeman who was killed elsewhere and the funeral was elsewhere and at another time, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Perhaps they did not understand when I was giving the statement. What I wanted to say was that there were too many events going on and this is why I was unable to recall them all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now allow me to return to the part of the question asked of you by the Prosecutor showing item 12 of your statement to you. It's on page 1D4526 of the English version. Let me now find the reference for the Macedonian version. It's 1D4540. As the entire paragraph was read out to you, as far as I remember, you said that part of it was wrong, and you mentioned the way or the road toward Volkovo, a village in the vicinity of Skopje. And you said that now, upon second thought, not everything that you stated under item 2 [as interpreted] was correct. Do you remember that you replied to the Prosecutor in this way?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you some questions about this. Today as you are testifying under oath, do you remember that on Sunday morning, you drove Minister Boskoski to a barber in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were in the barbershop where the minister was also present --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- and Branko Pejcinovski and the driver were in the car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you remember that at a certain time the driver brought a mobile phone to the minister or told him that President Trajkovski was on the line?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the section that was read out to you, is it correct that the minister, when answering the phone said, President, which to you meant that he was speaking to President Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you basically do not know what Minister Boskoski was discussing with President Trajkovski because you weren't listening to the minister's conversation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, actually, in the section that was read out to you what is wrong is only the information pertaining to your drive to Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: I said that I did not remember, but one cannot go through Ljubanci through Volkovo. We all know this. I have said this because I had to say something at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to say to you that after the conversation with the president of Macedonia, Minister Boskoski said that you should go to Ljubanci because something was happening there, would that be in line with the facts -- with the events of that morning; is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that after an hour and a half or so, you left for Ljubanci. Is it correct that after the barbershop you went to the Ministry of Interior to prepare for the departure for Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I now recall that we went back to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that two vehicles left, and apart from yourself there was also Branko Pejcinovski accompanying the minister for the -- Marian Medarov and Laste Mitkov?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You replied to my learned friend the Prosecutor that you couldn't comment what that journalist was saying but that you were -- you were taking care of the minister and not of the journalist. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, the many things that you don't remember have to do with your very duty to take care of the minister's security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The overall situation due to which you and your colleagues disregard other things is linked with your responsibility for the life of the person protected by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that you didn't know how the TV crew had come to -- had arrived?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say to you that Eli Cakar who was mentioned by the Prosecutor and who had stated that she had arrived in the minister's vehicle, you would have no reason to doubt that statement, but that you didn't remember -- you don't remember that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All your clarifications that you provided replying to the Prosecutor are closely linked with your duty as a body-guard and the great responsibility you had for the life and the security of the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at item 12 -- I apologise. No, I'm not going to ask this question now in order to save time. As you said that the part of your statement about going to Ljubanci by way of Volkovo and that you couldn't remember that, is it true that while giving the statement to the investigator you couldn't remember that you had stopped in front of a police station and that you were guided by an ethnic Albanian police officer from that station to Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: At that moment, I could not remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But when the investigator reminded you by asking you whether it was possible that someone had guided you, only then you remembered that there actually was a vehicle driving in front of you until the spot where you stepped out of the vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So all these examples I have now mentioned that are parts of your statement given to the investigators in 2004, corroborate, to my understanding, what you wanted to say today to this Chamber; namely, that you cannot remember at all many events and occurrences.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that for this reason, you may have said some things that are wrong; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA JAKOVOSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as I would now like to -- as I have some questions that are not directly connected to this, I wonder whether this might not be a good time for us to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn for the day, resuming tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.56 p.m.,
